blindSourceSummaries: Anti-trans national legal-risk assessment map, July 2026 edition (republished by advocacy media): places this state in its top protective grouping, alongside 14 states and the capital district, based on regional non-discrimination law and shield/refuge protections enforceable against out-of-state prosecutions; records the July 2026 shifts - one state became the fourth-ever travel-warning jurisdiction after a felony bathroom ban carrying up to 5-year sentences, another rose into the criminalisation grouping after extending its bathroom ban to universities - and describes the federal layer (passport sex-marker freeze, binary-only airline passenger data, funding withdrawals) behind its travel-warning advisory for non-essential travel by transgender people to the country as a whole.

Equality-map project on transgender healthcare 'shield'/refuge laws (data as of 25 September 2026): 16 states plus the capital district shield patients, families and providers of gender-affirming care from civil or criminal exposure created by other states' bans (covering 38% of the transgender population aged 13+); 2 more shield by executive order (6%); 32 states and 5 overseas territories have no such protection (56%). This state is among the shield-law jurisdictions underpinning that top protective rating.
blindLocalsOnly: The only recorded differences from peer protective states are health-insurance coverage details for gender-affirming care that apply to residents; a visitor never encounters them.
